title: What Robot Dividend Systems Is
definition: Robot Dividend Systems: sharing automation gains as dividends.
description:
Robot Dividend Systems: sharing automation gains as dividends. This is Post-Scarcity Economy at its most ambitious — robot taxes research, system logistics engineering and gain measurement operations converging on a single goal: making system hulls real.

Why it matters: Post-Scarcity Economy will decide payout design outcomes this century. Robot Dividend Systems is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working system hulls, the larger robot taxes vision stalls, and with it, the system logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Robot Dividend Systems in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Robot Dividend Systems
title: Real Research Today: Robot Dividend Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Robot Dividend Systems.
description:
The road to Robot Dividend Systems is already being paved. Platform cooperativism (Trebor Scholz) builds worker-owned digital platforms. Quadratic funding (Gitcoin) has distributed $60M+ to public goods via matching markets.

Data dividend proposals (California) argue users should be paid for their data. Together these programs form the robot taxes foundation that Robot Dividend Systems will build on — the system logistics results, the gain measurement methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Robot Dividend Systems
definition: Estimates Robot Dividend Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Robot Dividend Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Robot Dividend Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Robot Dividend Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Robot Dividend Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 44800 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where robot taxes monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or gain measurement maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Robot Dividend Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Robot Dividend Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Robot Dividend Systems — sharing automation gains as dividends.

Phase 1 — Prove (robot taxes): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (gain measurement): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (payout design): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and nations-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
